topic: Diagrid Durable Workflows for AI Agents Guide 2026

competitors.title: Diagrid Catalyst Documentation: Ship Reliable AI Agents and Workflows
key_points: Catalyst is an AI orchestration platform bringing durable workflows, access control, and governance to AI agents and MCP servers
Built on Dapr runtime (graduated CNCF project) — open foundation with SPIFFE identity, OTEL telemetry, Cloud Events
Works with any language, any framework (Dapr Agents, CrewAI, LangGraph, Strands, OpenAI Agents, Google ADK, Pydantic AI, Microsoft Agent Framework)
Deployment spectrum: Catalyst Cloud (fully managed), Enterprise Dedicated (single-tenant), Self-hosted (data plane in your cluster), Air-gapped (fully disconnected)
Key capabilities: durable execution, cryptographic agent identity, policy-based access control, workflow visualization

competitors.title: Durable Execution — Event Sourcing and Deterministic Replay
key_points: Durable execution via event sourcing (append-only history log) and deterministic replay — not checkpointing or snapshots
Every workflow step persisted: WorkflowStarted, ActivityScheduled, ActivityCompleted, TimerCreated, TimerFired, ExternalEventReceived
On crash, orchestrator re-runs from top replaying history — completed activities return recorded output without re-execution
30-day workflow with 200 activities resumes on fresh process in milliseconds via replay
Determinism requirement: no random numbers, UUIDs, current time, I/O, or blocking primitives in orchestrator code
Activities are the escape hatch for real-world I/O — each is atomic, recorded, and retried at-least-once (must be idempotent)
Continue-as-new bounds history for forever-running workflows (monitor loops, long-running agents)

competitors.title: Why AI Agents Fail in Production — The Four Failure Modes
key_points: Gartner predicted >40% of agentic AI projects will be canceled by end of 2027 due to escalating costs, unclear value, inadequate risk controls
S&P Global survey: average organization scrapped 46% of AI proofs of concept before production; companies abandoning most AI initiatives rose from 17% (2024) to 42% (2025)
MIT NANDA initiative: only ~5% of integrated AI pilots showed measurable bottom-line impact

Four failure modes: durability (no crash recovery), security (shared static credentials, no agent identity), cost (unpredictable token spend, double-billing on restarts), observability (non-deterministic workflows don't fit request-response monitoring)
Agent frameworks define behavior; Catalyst provides the production platform underneath — durability, identity, observability, cost control
Demo agents run on clean machines; production agents face pod reschedules, rate limits, database outages, security audits

competitors.title: Dapr 1.18: Securing and Hardening Workflows and Agents
key_points: Workflow History Context Propagation: downstream steps read ancestor execution history via typed API — Lineage (full chain) or OwnHistory (current only)

Workflow History Tamper Detection: cryptographic signing of history events using sidecar's mTLS X.509 SPIFFE identity — verifies chain linkage, event contiguity, digest recomputation, certificate validity
WorkflowAccessPolicy: allow-list semantics for which app IDs can invoke workflows/activities on a target app — authorizes by workflow name, activity name, and operation (schedule, terminate, etc.)
Workflow Concurrency Limits: Scheduler enforces global limits across all replicas — per-workflow and per-activity caps (e.g., max 5 SendEmail activities at once)

MCP Security: Option 1 — secure existing MCP servers transparently via service invocation access control; Option 2 — register MCP server as durable MCPServer resource with retries, persistence, and tamper-evident history
MCPServer resource supports streamable_http, sse, stdio transports; auth modes: static header, OAuth2 client credentials, SPIFFE JWT SVID injection

competitors.title: What's New in Catalyst: Failure Discovery, Human-in-the-Loop, Self-Hosted
key_points: Failure discovery: workflow graph shows failure percentages on each activity step — click to see filtered list of failed instances at that step
Bulk rerun: select affected instances, confirm starting step, rerun from point of failure — completed work stays completed, no duplicate side effects
Human-in-the-loop: discover workflows waiting on external events across all workflows or within a specific workflow type
Raise events directly from Catalyst UI to unblock waiting workflows — optional payload data, workflow code controls what happens next
Self-hosted deployment: single command `diagrid region deploy my-region` installs Catalyst data plane into your Kubernetes cluster
Air-gapped: both control plane and data plane run inside your infrastructure — no traffic leaves the network

competitors.title: Durable Agentic Workflows with Dapr — From Deterministic to Agentic
key_points: Deterministic workflows + LLM at edges = AI workflows (predictable orchestration, adaptable inputs)
Agent = goal-driven program that reasons, plans, and acts using LLMs + tools + memory in a loop
Agentic workflow = workflow created/managed by an agent — dynamically plans steps, executes, reflects, adjusts until goal achieved
DurableAgent class from Dapr Agents: every reasoning step, tool invocation, and workflow transition executed through Dapr's workflow runtime
Agent as local decision-maker, not global one — workflow defines business process, agent focuses on localized reasoning
Catalyst provides full visibility: every step, LLM call, and tool call inspectable with inputs and outputs

competitors.title: Durable Workflow Patterns: Chaining, Fan-out/Fan-in, Monitor, HITL, Compensation
key_points: Task Chaining: sequential steps with output passing — failed steps retry from that point, earlier steps not re-executed
Fan-out/Fan-in: parallel activity instances with when_all aggregation — bounded by worker pool, no manual concurrency management
Async HTTP: return HTTP 202 with instance ID, expose status endpoint — workflow runs durably in background regardless of pod recycling
Monitor: recurring loop with durable timer — wakes, checks condition, acts, repeats; supports continue-as-new for unbounded history
External System Interaction (HITL): pause for human approval with timeout — WaitForExternalEvent + durable timer + when_any
Compensation (Saga): track completed steps, run compensating activities in reverse order on failure — activities must be idempotent

competitors.title: Debugging Agents in Production with Catalyst
key_points: Dapr emits OTEL-compatible spans for every API call — workflow invocations, pub/sub, state operations, conversation API calls
Dapr Agents Python SDK instruments agent-specific behavior (LLM calls, tool invocations, reasoning chains) via OpenTelemetry with AgentObservabilityConfig
Catalyst Apps Graph shows live topology with error rate, P95 latency, and request rate per connection — derived from live telemetry
Workflow execution detail: visual DAG with color-coded nodes, step-level input/output/error/execution time, stack trace
Concrete debugging example: 429 quota exceeded error surfaced through workflow graph → step detail → error message → stack trace
Fix paths: retries with exponential backoff for rate limits, quota increase for exhaustion, Dapr resiliency policies for production

angles: Durable execution as the missing production layer: agent frameworks define behavior, but Catalyst provides the infrastructure that makes behavior survive crashes, restarts, and region failovers — the Kubernetes moment for AI agents

Four failure modes framework: durability (crash recovery), security (agent identity), cost (token spend predictability), observability (non-deterministic workflow tracing) — a diagnostic lens for any production agent deployment

Event sourcing vs checkpointing: Dapr's replay-based durability is fundamentally different from snapshot-based approaches — no serialized stack, no paused execution, just an append-only log that can reconstruct state in milliseconds

Deterministic orchestrator + non-deterministic activities: the architectural pattern that reconciles LLM unpredictability with production reliability — all I/O, randomness, and time-dependent operations go in activities
Agent identity as the new workload identity: SPIFFE-based cryptographic identity for agents parallels the shift from static API keys to mTLS in microservices — agents need passports, not shared keys
Human-in-the-loop as a first-class workflow primitive: WaitForExternalEvent + durable timers + Catalyst UI event raising turns approval workflows from instance-ID hunts into normal operator workflows
Multi-framework durability: Catalyst works with 9+ agent frameworks (CrewAI, LangGraph, OpenAI Agents, Google ADK, etc.) — durability is a platform property, not a framework feature

The cost-durability connection: without durable execution, every crash restarts from step 1, double-billing LLM tokens — 15-30% failure rates mean a significant share of the LLM bill pays for redoing completed work
